old_caption: The video captures a close-up view of a kitchen countertop, where a significant amount of white steam is billowing out from an unseen source. The steam is thick and dense, creating a swirling effect as it rises and spreads across the surface. The countertop is dark, possibly black or dark gray, which contrasts sharply with the bright white steam. In the background, various kitchen items are visible, including a white coffee mug with some text on it, a silver container, and other miscellaneous objects that suggest a typical kitchen setting. The lighting in the room appears to be natural, coming from a window or light source outside the frame, illuminating the scene and highlighting the steam's movement. There are no animals or characters present in the video; the focus remains solely on the steam and the surrounding kitchen environment. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, maintaining a consistent angle that captures the dynamic motion of the steam as it rises and disperses across the countertop.

caption: The video captures a stationary indoor kitchen view where a dense billow of white vapor already fills the central frame and keeps moving throughout the excerpt. Behind the cloud, a bright window on the left holds several bottles, including a blue-capped one, while a dark cabinet face occupies the lower-left and a glossy countertop on the right supports a metallic kettle lid and a pale mug bearing partial text. A thin horizontal line crosses the middle of the scene, remaining fixed and sometimes occluded by the drifting smoke. The vapor itself does not appear or vanish; instead its compact central mass gradually loosens, spreading outward as the left portion stretches further left and upward and a wispy tail extends toward the kettle. The cloud's core thins relative to its edges, giving an impression of slow diffusion and deformation rather than a single rigid translation. Background objects and their relative positions stay essentially unchanged, indicating no significant camera pan, tilt, or zoom, so the visible motion belongs to the vapor alone. The excerpt ends with the cloud still present and reshaping, its source and fate outside the captured range.
